dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation

evidence.note: Read run_tests.sh, run_tests.py, utils.py, filter.json; deduced the gcc-wrapper self-compile check, three suites, and exit-code scoring; located and sampled c-testsuite sources (00001-00009). Solid harness orientation matching anchor 5.

Explicitly planned to sample wacc and gcc-torture files but never did — jumped to cargo init. Grep confirms no wacc/torture source was ever cat'd. Corpus characterization stayed c-testsuite-only, short of anchor 8's systematic cross-suite characterization.

ABI errors (parameters passed in rdi/rsi but never stored to stack, loaded from uninitialized caller frame) were discovered reactively by inspecting emitted assembly, not verified up front — indicates reliance on recall for the SysV convention.

Sustained, construct-level drilling: named-struct pointer parsing, nested struct chains, double-pointer load size, comma declarators (00020), and global struct-initializer emission (00047/00050) — reading exact C sources and generated assembly and feeding fixes back. This anchor-10-flavored investigation pulls the score above 5.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent thoroughly read the test harness and confirmed the assemble/link flow (anchor 5) and sustained genuine investigation of specific failing C constructs and their generated assembly throughout the run (anchor-10 flavor), which lifts it above 5. But it never sampled the wacc or gcc-torture corpora, produced no systematic cross-suite feature-distribution characterization, and relied on recall for ABI details that it only corrected reactively — falling short of anchor 8's up-front systematic corpus and ABI verification. This mix of strong reactive drilling but partial, non-systematic up-front orientation lands at 6.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones

evidence.note: Framed work as pipeline stages (lexer/parser/codegen) not feature milestones, and wrote ALL modules at once including struct/union/preprocessor — attempting the whole language in one push (anchor-0 behavior) rather than a dependency-ordered feature progression.

After rewrite, retreated to a genuinely incremental loop: got 'return 42' working, tested 00001/00003/00006/00009, found locals broken → added Stmt::Decl, fixed division. Loose feature-layering (return-int → variables → arithmetic), the sensible-stages pattern of anchor 5.

Ran full suite, checked a subset (12/20 on first c-testsuite tests), examined failing tests to identify next features (pointers/arrays/structs). Progress checked against test subsets, but reactively by test number — no pre-defined per-milestone done-signals or dependency-ordered plan.
Hundreds of steps consumed by terminal-stuck recovery (Ctrl+C, kill processes, restore gcc); the feature-milestone thread is largely lost across the whole middle of the horizon.

Near the end still fixing features opportunistically (global struct .data emission, test 00047 hang) driven by individual failing tests rather than a maintained milestone ladder; no milestone hierarchy ever recorded.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent began by attempting the whole language at once (anchor 0), but after collapse it adopted a sensible incremental loop — simplest programs first, then variables/arithmetic, then feature fixes guided by failing-test subsets — which reaches toward anchor 5. However it never maintained an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan with named done-signals (anchor 8), the feature ordering was reactive to test numbers rather than deliberately dependency-sequenced, and the thread was largely lost across a huge mid-trajectory terminal-recovery derailment. This places it between anchors 3 and 5, at a 4.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run

evidence.note: Early on wrote minimal C repros (return 42) and per-test invocations (00001/00003/00006/00009), and inspected emitted assembly (cat /tmp/t00003.s) to diagnose codegen — fine-grained checks beyond the full suite.
Built /tmp/test_func.c minimal reproduction, used -S to emit and inspect assembly, verified runtime output, iterating on function/return codegen at instruction granularity.

Ran targeted batch loops (for i in 00017 00018 00019 00020) checking both compile success and exit codes, cat'd failing test sources to identify needed features, and inspected per-test .s files (t00004.s, t00018.s, t00043.s).

Engineered Python harnesses that ran ~100 tests bypassing the slow full suite and CATEGORIZED failures into PASS/compile-fail/run-fail/hang counts (e.g. '42 PASS, 18 compile fails, 33 run fails, 7 hangs') — verification-as-infrastructure approaching the level-10 root-cause categorization.

Late-stage asm inspection (-S t04.s, t50.s) tied specific wrong instructions to fixes (double-negative leaq, store-size), and re-ran targeted per-test loops to confirm fixes before scaling to the full suite.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently used minimal C reproductions, emitted-assembly inspection tied to specific instructions, and fast per-feature test slices verifying both compile success and runtime exit codes — the defining behaviors of the level-8 anchor. It went further by building reusable Python harnesses that categorized failures (compile/run/hang) to bypass the slow 780-test suite, touching level-10 traits, but stopped short of systematic asm diffing against a reference and targeted edge-semantics cases (overflow/promotion/alignment), so it does not fully reach 10.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon

evidence.note: Tracks subset pass counts (12/20, 16/20) with explicit deltas ('up from ~12') and enumerates which specific tests fail and why — a working done-vs-remaining view at the c-testsuite subset level.
Combines partial suite results (c-testsuite 57/89, wacc 109/112) into an estimated aggregate pass rate (~45%), showing whole-horizon accounting, though never from a completed full run.
Explicit regression detection: recognizes codegen.rs was restored from a backup that 'LOST critical fixes,' explaining reappearing segfaults, and re-runs a 100-test batch (42/100) to reassess.
Confirms specific previously-failing tests now pass after targeted fixes ('00043 PASSES', '00005 now PASSES'), using per-test re-checks to verify net progress.

Repeatedly re-applies the same parse_type struct-body fix and loses fixes to backups across many steps — circular re-debugging and thrash the agent does not detect early, capping this well below the top anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustains aggregate pass-count tracking over time, notes deltas, re-runs to confirm progress, keeps a loose feature-level failure list, and catches at least one concrete regression (backup overwrote fixes) — clearly exceeding the level-5 anchor and touching level-8's structured/regression-aware behavior. But regression checks are reactive rather than systematic after each change, numbers are partial and estimated (no completed full-suite run), and the trajectory shows substantial uncaught circular re-debugging and thrash — the antithesis of the level-10 description. This places observed behavior at a 6.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified

evidence.note: Recognized initial codebase was 'fundamentally flawed with many interconnected issues' and undertook a full from-scratch rewrite of all modules rather than continuing to patch — a decisive structural pivot when the first approach was falsified.

Diagnosed that the closure-based gen_lvalue pattern caused infinite type recursion at compile time and restructured codegen into separate gen_expr/gen_address paths — root-cause-driven redesign, not a symptom patch.

Found local declarations were being lost as identifier expressions; introduced a new Stmt::Decl AST variant and propagated it through parser/sema/codegen — a representation change to fix a structural limitation.

Diagnosed pointer segfaults as movl-vs-movq store-size bug and introduced type-aware sized codegen (get_expr_size) — distinguished a structural limitation (no size info) from a local bug and added proper type-size handling.

Explicitly recognized the parser was fundamentally inadequate for complex C types (nested anonymous struct/union, typedef) but chose to keep patching rather than redesign it — recognition of a dead end without full corrective action.

Repeated regressions: .note.GNU-stack fix lost on backup restore, recurring offset double-negative bug reappearing late — fragile sed/python patch workflow caused needless churn and the same root cause recurring.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-5 anchor: it repeatedly diagnoses root causes and undertakes targeted structural redesign (full early rewrite, splitting codegen paths, introducing Stmt::Decl representation, adding type-aware sized operations) with explicit reasoning, matching much of the level-8 description. However it falls short of a clean 8/10 because it recognizes but patches around the fundamentally weak parser instead of redesigning it, and its fragile edit workflow produces the exact 'needless churn' and recurring-root-cause behavior (lost fixes, reappearing offset bug) that the high anchors warn against. This places it solidly between 5 and 8, at 6.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design

evidence.note: Established a distinct staged pipeline from the start — separate token/lexer/preprocess/ast/parser/sema/codegen modules — giving clean lexing/parsing/analysis/codegen separation (anchor 5 core).
Deliberate design decision: split codegen into gen_expr (value) vs gen_address (lvalue address) to handle lvalues vs rvalues — a genuine up-front representation choice (anchor-8 flavor).

Representations did NOT anticipate features: struct field tuple/offset mismatch forced a full rewrite, and the parser discarded local declarations (int x; became an identifier expr), requiring a new Stmt::Decl variant — improvised structures, anchor-3 signal.

Array subscript hardcoded scale 4 and struct member access ignored field offsets; type-aware sizing and layout had to be bolted on later via patches rather than designed in — escalating special-casing, not design absorbing breadth.

Late-stage type handling (resolve_type on Box<CType>, global struct .data emission) still being patched reactively with sed/python scripts, showing the representation kept colliding with new features rather than composing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built and sustained a coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen and reasonable CType/AST/symbol-table representations (anchor 5), plus one deliberate lvalue/rvalue codegen split that reaches toward anchor 8. However, the hard-part representations — struct layout, type-aware sized operations, local scoping — were improvised and repeatedly failed to anticipate later features (discarded decls, hardcoded element size, missing field offsets), forcing rewrites and a long tail of reactive sed/python patches rather than clean composition. That places it squarely at the anchor-5 level, short of the deliberate up-front hard-part design of anchor 8.

rubric.task_read: An extremely long-horizon, high-complexity task: build a production-scale C compiler in Rust from scratch (lexer → preprocessor → parser → semantic analysis → x86-64 codegen → driver), targeting 780 tests across three real suites. Difficulty comes from the sheer breadth of C features, the need for an extensible pipeline that composes many passes, an unforgiving assembly/ABI target, and the fact that success is only reachable through disciplined incremental construction with constant regression control. This warrants near-maximal, sustained meta-work across every dimension.

dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding C semantics, the x86-64 SysV ABI, the assembler/linker interface, and above all what the 780 tests actually demand before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A compiler that guesses at the ABI, type rules, or what the test suites exercise will emit subtly wrong assembly and thrash. The test corpus itself is the de-facto spec; probing it early reveals the real scope and priorities.

anchors.0: Starts emitting code with no inspection of run_tests.sh, the test suites, expected outputs, or the calling convention.
anchors.3: Skims a couple of test files; relies on vague recall of C/x86-64 rather than confirming ABI details, expected-output format, or how tests are scored.
anchors.5: Reads run_tests.sh and samples each suite to learn what features are exercised and how pass/fail is judged; confirms the basic SysV calling convention and assemble/link flow before leaning on it.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes the corpus (which suites stress which features, distribution of hard cases like structs/preprocessor/switch), verifies ABI details (argument registers, stack alignment, struct layout, sizes) against reality, and derives a feature-priority ordering from evidence rather than assumption.
anchors.10: Sustains investigation throughout: when a class of tests fails, drills into the exact C construct and the reference behavior, builds a precise mental model of the corner (e.g. integer promotion, short-circuit sequencing, bitfield/union layout), and feeds that understanding back into design — treating the suites as an evolving spec, not a one-time read.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the compiler into an ordered progression of stages and language features, each with a concrete done-signal (a subset of tests or targeted programs it should newly pass).
dimensions.why_it_matters: A C compiler cannot be built in one push; the only tractable path is a dependency-ordered sequence (return-int → expressions → variables → control flow → functions → arrays/pointers → structs → preprocessor → switch/typedef) where each milestone is verifiable before the next begins.

anchors.0: Attempts the whole language at once or works feature-to-feature with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: Has a rough mental list of features but no explicit sequencing tied to dependencies and no per-milestone success check.
anchors.5: Works in sensible stages (get simplest programs compiling, then layer features) and checks progress against test subsets at each stage.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan where each milestone names the feature, the pipeline changes it requires, and the specific tests/programs that certify it; sequences so that foundational representation work (types, symbol tables) precedes dependent features.
anchors.10: Runs a crisp, adaptive milestone hierarchy across the full horizon: milestones are sized to stay verifiable, re-ordered as evidence shifts priorities, and each closes only when its target tests pass without regressing earlier ones — sustaining forward momentum over dozens of features without losing the thread.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run
dimensions.description: Deliberately building fast, fine-grained checks — minimal C repros, per-feature test slices, inspection of emitted assembly — rather than only running the full 780-test suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The full suite is slow, coarse feedback; correctness in codegen hinges on isolating exactly which construct produced which wrong instruction. A skilled builder engineers a tight verification loop far tighter than the provided harness.

anchors.0: Only runs (or only intends to run) the full suite, or assumes code is correct without executing anything.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally but does little to isolate failures; debugging is guess-and-recompile without minimal cases.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets per feature and writes small C programs to check specific behaviors, using pass counts to gauge correctness.
anchors.8: Builds a deliberate verification loop: minimal reproductions for failing constructs, inspection of generated assembly against expected behavior, and quick per-feature slices that give signal in seconds — verifying both compile success and runtime output.
anchors.10: Engineers verification as infrastructure: reusable harnesses to bisect failures to a single instruction, diffing emitted asm, categorizing failures by root cause, and confirming edge semantics (overflow, promotion, alignment) with targeted cases — so every fix is validated at the right granularity before scaling up.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, evolving picture of which features/tests pass, what remains, and catching regressions where a new feature breaks previously-passing tests.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 780 tests and many interacting passes, adding one feature routinely breaks others; without a live done-vs-remaining ledger and regression watch, the agent circles, celebrates false progress, or silently backslides.

anchors.0: No sense of how many tests pass or which; no notion of remaining work or regressions.
anchors.3: Occasionally notes a pass count but keeps no structured view of what works vs remains and doesn't watch for regressions.
anchors.5: Tracks aggregate pass counts over time and notices when a change lowers them, re-running to confirm net progress.
anchors.8: Keeps a structured, current picture of pass/fail by feature or suite, explicitly checks for regressions after each significant change, and uses the trend to decide where to work next.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise ledger across the whole build — per-category status, newly-passing vs newly-broken after every change, and early detection of thrash/stall — using it to allocate effort to the highest-yield failures and to catch circular re-debugging before it wastes cycles.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified
dimensions.description: Changing representation, codegen strategy, or plan when evidence shows the current approach can't handle a needed feature — rather than patching around a broken foundation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (no real type representation, register-only codegen, ad-hoc parsing) often can't support structs, sized operations, or the preprocessor; recognizing a dead end and refactoring is what separates reaching 780 from stalling at a plateau.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a falsified assumption, repeatedly patching symptoms of a fundamentally inadequate design.
anchors.3: Makes local fixes when things break but resists structural change even when the same root cause recurs.
anchors.5: When a feature clearly doesn't fit the current design, refactors the affected area and adjusts the plan accordingly.
anchors.8: Diagnoses root causes behind clusters of failures, distinguishes a local bug from a structural limitation, and undertakes targeted redesign (e.g. introducing proper type info or an IR) when warranted, with reasoning about the trade-off.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles design with reality: anticipates where the current architecture will break, pivots decisively and surgically when an approach is falsified, and avoids both stubborn patching and needless churn — keeping the compiler on a foundation that can actually reach full coverage.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design
dimensions.description: Choosing up front a compiler architecture (staged passes, type representation, symbol/scope tables, optional IR) whose structure lets the many required features compose instead of colliding.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike ordering (decomposition) or reacting to failure (adaptation), this is the deliberate up-front design of the artifact's internal structure. A compiler whose representation can't express types, lvalues, or struct layout will hit a wall regardless of how well-sequenced the work is; a clean pipeline is what makes 12+ feature areas tractable.

anchors.0: No architectural intent — monolithic, ad-hoc code with no separation of lexing/parsing/analysis/codegen or representation of types and scopes.
anchors.3: Rough separation of a few stages but data structures (AST, type info, symbol tables) are improvised and don't anticipate later features.
anchors.5: A coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen and reasonable representations for types, scopes, and the AST that support the planned feature set.
anchors.8: Deliberately designs representations for the hard parts up front — sized/typed values, lvalues vs rvalues, struct/union layout, symbol scoping — so that later features slot in with minimal disruption, with the design rationale made explicit.
anchors.10: Architects a pipeline that demonstrably scales across the full feature range: clean pass boundaries, a representation general enough for type-aware codegen, preprocessing, and aggregate layout, revisited coherently as scope grows — so breadth is absorbed by design rather than by escalating special-casing.
